title: Gullwing shift handoff tidbits
content:
Quick informal handoff notes — not polished, meant for the next night shift. Keep this file open on the tablet.

Shift summary (2300-0700):
- Quiet first half; normal traffic. Minor spike at 01:14 UTC (frontend retry loop) — tied to client SDK version mismatch. Resolved by rolling back rate-limit rule in edge-lb (see ticket INC-2989).
- 03:22 UTC: transient KV cache pressure on eu-west-1 serving pool — observed 5s tail latency for small chat requests for ~7 minutes. No errors, just token latencies.
- 05:50 UTC: alert flapping for model-route fallback; Canary failed to fetch quantized weights on node gpu-09 (OOM during load). Automated fallback worked but we lost warm cache.

Open items / things to watch:
- KV cache pressure root cause unknown. Memory under pressure? Task: watch "realtime.kvstore.evictions_total" and "realtime.kvstore.kv_size_bytes" graph on the console. If evictions spike > 200/min, scale pool to +2 instances and notify infra.
- gpu-09 instability: hardware trace shows occasional ECC corrections. Set node to draining for next maintenance window if ECC counts keep rising.
- Canary model fallback recurrence: logs point to quantization loader failing on that node due to library mismatch after last OS patch (see PR link). Follow up with infra release team in morning.

Immediate actions I did:
- Temp: bumped serving pool (eu-west-1-chat) by +1 at 03:30 UTC — latency normalized.
- Rolled back edge rate-limit rule that caused client retries at 01:20 UTC. Left a comment in the rate-limit rule config (see linked PR).
- Marked gpu-09 as "investigate" in node-tracker and added tag "unstable".

Commands & quick snippets (save these in memory):
- tails: kubectl -n realtime logs -l app=kvstore -c kvstore --since=10m | grep Evicted
- metrics: curl -s "https://metrics.internal.redwood/realtime/graph?m=realtime.kvstore.evictions_total&span=15m" | jq .
- drain node: gcloud compute instances set-scheduling gpu-09 --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE (confirm with infra)
- list serving pods: kubectl -n realtime get pods -l pool=eu-west-1-chat -o wide

Notes to next person (to self):
- If latency returns after scaling, check trace prefix sampling: sometimes long traces are due to a new background eval job hitting the same pool (pid: eval-runner). There is a cron that runs at 03:00 UTC occasionally misconfigured; see cron-job eval-runner@infra.
- Do not restart the whole kvstore cluster unless you have explicit approval from on-call lead — rolling restarts only.

Short troubleshooting checklist (5 min triage):
1) Confirm alert details and symptom (metrics + logs)
2) Check recent deploys (gitops) and infra changes (Opsbot logs)
3) If memory/evictions, scale +1 instance, observe 3 min
4) If pod OOMs, capture core and open INC with screenshots
5) If node hardware ECC, tag and escalate to infra.

Followups / tickets to create next business day:
- Create a reproducible stress test for KV eviction patterns (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- PR to pin quantization library version on image builds to prevent loader mismatch (owner: applied-ml).
- Hardware check request for gpu-09 (owner: infra-support).

Loose thoughts & hypotheses (notes to self):
- Evictions might be due to eviction policy + new larger embedding cache entries introduced by the rerankers last week. Maybe reduce default prefix caching for rerank model.
- Warmup hooks for dedicated nodes are sometimes skipped when fallback triggers; consider adding prefetch step in fallback codepath.

Stuff I scribbled and didn't have time to tidy:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0XXXXXX/p1700XXXXX (watch for reply from @lena)
- Possible quick mitigation: enable per-route small-cache TTL 30s for rerank endpoints (test on staging).

If you read nothing else, do this in the first 10 minutes:
- Check kvstore evictions graph for last 60m. If spikes > 50/min, scale eu-west-1-chat +1. If node gpu-09 ECC corrections > 0 in last 24h, set to drain.

End of shift signature: Maya S. (left coffee in the frig)
summary: Personal on-call handoff scratchpad covering a KV cache pressure incident, a GPU node instability, commands, and follow-ups. Draft style, for next night SRE.
